linetext: PRESIDENT:  Good morning, everybody.
This is Day 2 of the hearing.
We're a few minutes early, but given we're all ready
to go, let's go.
I think there's a few bits of housekeeping to deal
with.
I received overnight the time allocation which has
been agreed, so thank you for that, together with a list
of attendees at yesterday's hearing.
I also acknowledge receipt of the application for
disclosure of documents in the main contract
proceedings.
Mr Hussain, no doubt you'll let us know when you're
able to respond to that application.
Is that something you can give us a time indication
for later today?
MR HUSSAIN:  Yes, sir, I will.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you very much.
I think, Mr Hussain, you're also going to let us
know about addendum 1 and the additional documents in
the bundle.
MR HUSSAIN:  Yes.  So Mr Gibbons (inaudible), we have no
objection to it.  We're happy for that to go in.
I think the addendum was already admitted.  We had some
consequential time allowance on that.
Sorry, I'll let you proceed.
PRESIDENT:  Fine.  That's fine.
MR HUSSAIN:  Sir, on my list you asked yesterday for the
date of termination.  My understanding is it took effect
on 5 February 2018, which is 14 days after 22 January.
My understanding is that's the same date in both
sides' chronologies, {G4-4} and {G9-4}, so my
understanding is 5 February.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you for that confirmation.  We'll work to
5 February 2018.
Unless there's any housekeeping from the claimant?
MR HICKEY:  No, sir, thank you.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you very much, in which case I think we
have Mr Ul Haq.
MR HICKEY:  Yes, with your permission, I call my factual
witness, Mr Ameen Ul Haq.
MR MUHAMMAD AMEEN UL HAQ
MR HICKEY:  The affirmation text is on the table with his
witness statement in front of him and it's clean.
WITNESS:  Good morning.
PRESIDENT:  Good morning, Mr Ul Haq.  Would you please
confirm your full name for the record.
WITNESS:  Mohammad Ameen Ul Haq.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you very much.  It's been agreed in this
arbitration that witnesses of fact will make an
affirmation and you should see, both on the screen and
on the piece of paper before you, the words of an
affirmation.  Do you have that?
WITNESS:  Yes, I have the paper in front of me.
PRESIDENT:  Would you please read out and give your
affirmation.
WITNESS:  I solemnly and sincerely declare that I shall
speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the
truth.  I understand that the evidence that I am about
to give is my own evidence and must not be influenced by
any other person.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you very much.
Mr Hickey will now take you to your evidence.
Examination-in-chief by MR HICKEY
MR HICKEY:  Good morning, Mr Ul Haq.  Do you like to be
called Mr Ul Haq or Mr Ameen?  Which do you prefer?
A.  Both ways is okay.  I prefer to be called Ameen.
Q.  Mr Ameen.  It's probably easier for everyone.
In front of you, you should have a witness statement
bundle.  Could I ask you please first to turn to page
{D4} of the hard copy.  It may also appear in front of
you on the electronic screen.
Do you recognise that document as your first witness
statement?
A.  Yes.
Q.  If I could ask you to please turn to page 24.  Is that
your signature underneath the statement of truth?
A.  Yes, this is my signature.
Q.  Before I go to the errata about that, you also gave
a further witness statement, I believe.  Could I ask you
to look at {D3}.  Do you recognise that as a reply
witness statement that is yours?
A.  Yes, this is mine.
Q.  If I can ask you to look at page 3, can you confirm that
that is your signature there?
A.  Yes, this is my signature.
Q.  Have you read those witness statements recently?
A.  Yes, I have read recently the witness statements.
Q.  I'm not sure whether it's in hard copy form in front of
you, but -- it is.  Could you turn to {D6a}.  I think
this is a list of corrections to your witness
statements; is that right?
A.  Yes, exactly.
Q.  If you turn over the page, just flick through to page 2
and 3.
So you've set out those corrections.  Subject to
those corrections, Mr Ameen, are the content of your
witness statement true and the evidence you wish to give
to the tribunal?
A.  Yes, the contents are true, subject to this errata
sheet, and the entire witness statement, remaining part,
are all true.
Q.  Mr Ameen, it's a very large room and I'm used to doing
it in large rooms.  The microphone in front of you does
not amplify your voice.  But it is essential that you,
as it were, speak into the microphone, so that the
transcribers can hear your words.
But also if you could try to keep your voice up,
because Mr Hussain, who's going to ask you some
questions in a moment, will not be able to hear you if
you are speaking quite softly and there's air
conditioning as well.
A.  I will do my best.
MR HICKEY:  And also the members of the tribunal would like
to hear what you have to say, too.
So with that, I'll hand you over to Mr Hussain.  He
will then ask you some questions.
Cross-examination by MR HUSSAIN
MR HUSSAIN:  Mr Ameen, good morning.
A.  Good morning.
Q.  If we can go to your witness statement, {D4-3},
paragraph 11 of your first statement, you say that you
were DAR's designated point of contact for all
commercial and contractual matters with CQBC on the
project; correct?
A.  Correct.
Q.  You weren't acting as a planner or a programmer;
correct?
A.  No.
Q.  You were not a project manager; correct?
A.  No.
Q.  You're not a designer or involved in shop drawings
submittals?
A.  No.
Q.  And then if we go to paragraph 9 of the same document,
you say that in the period between June 2021
and November 2023, you left DAR and you were working at
UCC in Saudi.  Then you say you returned to DAR at
a quantity surveyor manager in November 2023.  Have you
been assigned to projects or are you mostly assisting
with claims, arbitrations?
A.  After rejoining Dar Al Rokham, my job is to review the
context, work on the variations and the claims.  For the
ongoing project, the projects which are upcoming, the
contract review is required.  Apart from these
responsibilities, one of my responsibilities is to
follow up the arbitration case because I was the one who
was involved during the project.
Q.  Other people on the project, like the project managers
or the planners, et cetera, they're still at DAR, to
your knowledge, or have they moved on?
A.  Mr Mohammad Barakat has left, Mr Khalil Gomaa left.  The
planning manager, Abdulrahman Alharthi, he also left.
Mr Muaied Hasan is available.
Q.  Just remind me who Mr Muaied Hasan is.  What was his
designation?
A.  At that time, he was project manager.  Now he's the
general manager.
Q.  If we go to page 12 of your witness statement,
paragraph 50 you say:
"From the start of the Project, we ran into problems
that were outside DAR's control.  We sent many letters
to CQBC, often with photographs, so that CQBC could
resolve these issues, and DAR's works could progress
smoothly.  The main problems faced by DAR were as
follows ..."
Then you list some perceived problems.
If we just look at that, so we've got that paragraph
at page 12, we go to the next page.  Just trying to see
the length of your evidence on this.  You have page 13,
and then next page, page 14.  So you have spent about
two and a half pages talking about letters with
complaints of problems.
It's fair to say, isn't it, that you haven't looked
at the detail of how the project progressed; you've just
tried to give examples of correspondence?
A.  We as Dar Al Rokham are a subcontractor.  We work
together.  The quantity surveyor, project manager,
planners, design team, we are a small group, maximum say
15 or 16 people who were doing all the decision.  When
a matter come that affect the commercial thing or
contractual thing, definitely they consult me.
Like for example, if there are damages happening at
site and they ask me to submit a cost impact, I need to
go there to see that is it correct or not?  Likewise for
other item related to the access issues at the project.
The issue came, like the invoicing was going down,
resources were available at the project.  So I might
have to check what happened, why my QS is evaluating
very less work.
So I was visiting the site for these purposes, to
assess the payment application of my labour suppliers,
who were paid on unit rate basis, and to assess our own
payment to do the variation, and sometimes I was just
wandering around the site to understand what's going on.
Q.  Mr Ul Haq, it's important that you try and focus on the
question I put to you.
Firstly, you agree that you address these problems
in two and a half pages of your witness statement and
then there's an appendix that runs to about four pages;
correct?  That's where you deal with these issues?
A.  Correct, yes.
Q.  And you have just given some examples of letters.
You've not looked at the detail of the progress, yes?
You have just tried to give examples of letters in these
few pages?
A.  In few pages, according to the chronology, I have put
some letters to show the general appearance.  The total
correspondence are in thousands.
Q.  If we, for example, look at -- if we go to {D5-1}, which
is the appendix to your statement, description of
documents.  This document runs to four pages and you
list some letters there, 23 letters in total.  If we
look at the first page, you list three letters in 2014
and then it jumps to January 2016.  Then you have two
letters in early January 2016, and if we go over the
page, the remainder of the letters you mention are in
Again, you've just given some examples, you've not
looked at every week or every month or any detail of the
progress, yes?
A.  Yes, I was not recording the progress.  My job was
a quantity surveying job.  The progress report,
disruption, delays, these were the planners who were
doing it.
Q.  Thank you.  That's very fair.
So if we go to, for example, {D4-13}, and we see
paragraph 50.6, you talk about area clearances.
If we look at the middle of this paragraph, you say:
"These site access issues were notified to CQBC in
various letters including ..."
And then you list a number of letters in 2014 and
then, I think, four letters from July 2017; is that
correct?
A.  Yes, that's correct.
Q.  Did someone suggest you refer to these letters or you
just picked some examples?
A.  The issue of area clearances was impacting our payment
application --
Q.  Sorry, just answer the question.  Did someone suggest
you refer to these particular letters or did you pick
these examples yourself?
A.  I picked the example myself from the correspondence log.
Q.  Is there a reason why you've only referenced letters in
2014 and then from July 2017 or is that just random?
A.  In July 2017, or 2017 I would say, the work progress was
very slow and my visit to the project site was more
frequent.  So my memories and the involvement in the
letter in 2017 was much more as compared to 2015 and
2016.  In 2015 the project was running with full swing.
I was extremely busy in the variations, payment
applications, subcontract material order.  In 2017, the
work was almost stagnant.  It was on hold.  So by that
time my visit at the project was more, so that's why the
letter I'm referring for 2017 are more.
Q.  That's really helpful.  You're already told me that you
were a quantity surveyor and you weren't the main person
dealing with progress.  But even within that limitation,
your point is that you're not really aware of the
correspondence in 2015, 2016; you've really focused on
2017.  Is that fair?
A.  I was reading the correspondences for the entire project
duration.  But after reading the correspondence to go
back to the site, see what's going on there, in 2015, it
was less frequent.  My office work was more.  In 2017
the office work was almost nil.  So my visit at the
project was much more.
Q.  That's really helpful.  Thank you.
So for example, if we take -- just staying on this.
50.6, you reference a document.  Just bear with me one
second, make sure I have the right reference.  (Pause)
At {C227}, that's the document dated 16 July 2014,
this is:
"Site Clearance for Thermal Insulation & Stone
Cladding Building H03 East Elevation Recess Area at
Level 3 to Roof."
I mean, you haven't looked at whether this building
H03 was critical at that time, it's just an example you
have given from the letters; correct?
A.  Correct.
Q.  Thank you.  That's very helpful.
So who at DAR would have been in charge of
internally tracking and reporting progress of the works?
A.  The work progress was reported by the planning
department.  Initially, Mr Ahmad Annan(?) was there.
Then once he left, Mr Abdulrahman Alharthi, he was
there.
Q.  I mean, you may not know the answer to this, but I'm
expecting that there would be daily, weekly and monthly
records of what was being done on the site at different
elevations, at different levels within elevation and so
on.  All these progress records would exist, yes?
A.  Yes, these records were existing on the project.  Some
are still available, some we lost.
Q.  Sorry.  What do you mean some you lost?
A.  The first record at the project was from the
construction team.  They have A1 size drawings where
they were highlighting day-to-day basis the tile they
have fixed.  This was the original record.
Then from this record, we were making our payment,
planners were filling their own schedule of work.  So
this record was available on the construction site
itself.  They make a Portakabin.  It was there.
At the time of termination, we were not aware that
CQBC is terminated.  We did not take the item from
there.  On 5 February 2018, TCCC took over the site and
they cleaned, they demolish all the facility there.  As
a result, we lost some of our computers and these
original data, which was the site record, was also lost.
Q.  Let's just take that in stages.  That's not something
you mention in your witness statement, Mr Ameen.  When
you mention these letters, you don't say: actually,
there's some records, but they've been lost because they
were taken from a Portakabin on 5 February 2018.  You
don't say that; correct?
A.  No, if I remember, I did not write it in the written
witness statement.  For the IT record I wrote, IT server
record.
Q.  You say that this happened on 5 February 2018.  What are
you now saying happened on 5 February 2018?
A.  On 5 February 2018, when we enter into the project, the
project was taken over by TCCC.  We were not allowed to
enter.  I was there personally.  I was unable to enter
to the office where I was working there.  The area was
completely barricaded.  Then the site team told that
they are also not allowed to enter.
Once we came back on after, if I remember, two or
three days, so what we found in the project area office,
the IT server is not available, our desks are empty,
there is nothing there, and at the project site, all
Portakabins were demolished, the area is now clean.  So
any property which we had, it is lost.  We complained to
TCCC.  They told that you shall be aware that your
contractor is terminated.  But we were not aware of
that.
Q.  Sorry.  Let's just take that in stages.
Is it your evidence that there were, what, hard copy
documents in a Portakabin or computers?  What are you
saying was destroyed now?
A.  The computer server was in the project office.  Project
office was a big Portakabin where upper stair Carillion
staff was there, down the stair many subcontractor was
there.  At the project site where the construction was
going on, in the building, they make a site office with
Portakabin.  With plywood or Portakabin, these are
temporary sitting, where they are keeping the record on
day-to-day basis, they're highlighting the drawing with
colour pencils, writing any remark, like if the tile has
to be removed they will put a cross there, when they
will fix it, they will put a date.  So this was the --
you can say, mother record, this the original thing
happened.
Then at the project office, our planner and QS, they
were relying on this record to fill their schedule, like
when my QS Roshan is making payment application, he was
getting these drawings, like five building in one day,
then at the evening he will return it.  Then next day he
will get more drawing.  So by this way, he was making
payment.  The planners were making monthly progress in
the same way.
Q.  Just so I understand, you're saying that hard copy
documents in the Portakabin were destroyed by TCCC.  Is
that what you're saying now?
A.  I'm referring only the drawings which were kept by the
site team as a daily progress report.
Q.  In hard copy or online?
A.  It was hard copy, printed copy.
Q.  Are you saying that your understanding is TCCC destroyed
those documents?
A.  They destroyed.  They remove all the Portakabin from
there.
Q.  Do you have any records of you writing to TCCC saying,
"Where are our documents, why have you destroyed our
documents?"
A.  Once we came back, we sit with TCC and Msheireb, we
protested, and they responded that you shall be aware
that you are going to be terminated, your main
contractor is going to be terminated; you shall remove
any important thing at the project site.  But we were
not aware.
Q.  Sorry, I'm just asking you, again, did you write, put in
writing any time saying to TCCC, "You have destroyed our
documents"?
A.  No, there is no written evidence available for that.
Q.  You were well aware before 5 February 2018 that
a termination was coming of CQBC, were you?
A.  We were not aware at all.  What we noticed that the
presence of CQBC is almost nil.  There were only few
people.  They start demobilisation from April 2017,
March or April, when I see the QS department is now
going to be less populated and remaining department as
well.  From March 2017 up to their termination, they
almost demobilise from the project.
Q.  I'm going to look at what your communications were with
TCCC in a moment.
Just so I understand, they will be -- you may not
know this.  Just remind me, the gentleman Mr Ahmad that
you said was in charge of tracking and reporting
programmes, are you aware of whether there are daily,
weekly and monthly records of progress across the site?
A.  Yes, I am aware.  They were maintaining daily record and
they were reporting on weekly basis to CQBC.  There was
an agreed format, elevation by elevation, level by
level, the way how it should be reported on weekly
basis.  If I recall, it was Tuesday of every week when
they were reporting to them.
Q.  You still have those records or DAR will still have
them?
A.  Not all.  It is scattered.
Q.  Have you looked for them?  Or is that not a level of
detail that you have enquired into?  Have you looked for
them, Mr Ameen?  Or is that a level of detail that you
have not been asked to consider?
A.  The weekly report, I have gone through that one.  It has
building wise sections.  In each building, the
elevations are divided.  On each elevation, the level is
divided.  So this format, they were using it to report
on weekly basis.  Few of these weekly reports I have
seen, but many of them are not available because of the
loss of the server.
Q.  You continued the works for TCC under a letter of
intent.
A.  Yes, we continued.
Q.  So you would have had access to your server to continue
the works.
A.  The server was removed by them.  There was the server
was -- Dar Al Rokham, the CQBC, all the server -- it was
a single room for server, where internet was coming and
everybody was keeping the server.  The room was empty
when we reached there.
Q.  Sorry, I'm just going to ask again, just so we
understand.  You've not mentioned this in your witness
statement, we've already established that, yes?
A.  For IT server, if I recall, I mentioned that we lost our
IT server there.
Q.  You've not mentioned that the progress records were lost
at any stage from this Portakabin.  That's the first
time I think you've ever mentioned that.
A.  This one might be I did not write it in my witness
statement, but this is what happened for the drawings.
Q.  You've not provided any document where you complain to
TCCC that you don't have access to your progress records
or the server containing those records?
A.  You mean as a complaint to TCCC.
Q.  Yes?
A.  There is no written thing to them.
Q.  There's no internal records.  I mean if this happened
you would have written to your management and said,
"We've lost our records, what can we do?"  Is there any
internal record that you've provided?
A.  Internal record, yes, internal communication, our
project manager -- by that time Mr Muaied -- reported to
the office in Dubai what happened exactly on 5 February.
Q.  But you haven't provided that report with your evidence?
A.  It was in the form of an email which he provided.
Q.  You haven't provided that email with your evidence?
A.  No, it's not part of my witness statement.
Q.  When you continued the works in January, February,
March 2018 and thereafter, you would have needed access
to the server; correct?
A.  Once TCCC came, they changed all the methodology of
construction, even the CSI code were changed after they
came.  They told us: stop what you were doing before.
I don't need the continuation of same progress report or
same QA/QC log.  They sit with us and started everything
from zero.
Q.  Mr Ameen, again, I'm just going to ask a question quite
carefully.  The documents you had on that server will
need to be accessed by different people.  They're not
just in an off-line computer.  They would be available
to you through an online system, yes?
A.  It was available as long as I'm at site.  The server was
not online, what we call the LAN server, when you
connect few computer with the server, you cannot access
it when you are outside of that network.  It was that
kind of server.
Q.  Is there anywhere a list or a record of what documents
are said to have been lost that you have seen?  This is
the first time that I'm hearing that these documents
were lost.  Has anyone in DAR, to your knowledge -- you
may not know because you're working as an estimator or
QS.  Has anyone, to your knowledge, at DAR made a list
of progress records that have been lost?
A.  The progress reports which were lost, the weekly
reports, we did not make any list.  The items which are
available which we tried to recover are available.  But
what is lost, what is balance, there is no such list of
the project document.  Correspondences, yes, we have.
Q.  Sorry, sir, how do you have the correspondences?  Just
explain that to me.  Where are they kept?
A.  The correspondences were kept in the computer of the
document controller, not on the server.  So that's why
the correspondences survive and the as-built drawing and
shop drawing.  These were in the computer of the
drafting lead, the design lead, Mr Biju(?).  That one
survived.
The commercial-related data, it was in my laptop.
Many of it survive.  But my colleague Roshan, he had
a desktop.  His desktop gone.  So data was scattered by
that time.
Q.  So there is a document management, document control
system for the project; correct?
A.  There was a document controller on the project.
Q.  Just explain to me.  You have an online system which
keeps all the document control on there?
A.  Our system was not online.  Our server was used only
when we are at the project.  CQBC has an online
dedicated electronic data management system called
project -- 4P Projects.  This was used to communicate
between the main contractor, Msheireb, and the
consultant.
Q.  You just mentioned your document controller.  What
documents do they have or you don't know?
A.  The document controller main job was to keep the record
of the correspondences, the letters which are incoming
and outgoing, and the transmittals.
Q.  If we can go to {C-872}, this is a letter dated
8 April 2018.
If you can just see the whole document, it's signed
by Mr Hasan.  It's addressed to Teyseer Contracting
Company Consolidated Contractors Group JV, which we call
TCCC.
Were you involved in preparing this letter?
A.  Yes, I was involved.  I was coordinating with Mr Barakat
on this matter.
Q.  Sorry, just remind me, who is Mr Barakat?
A.  He was the commercial manager in Dubai, my senior.
Q.  At DAR?
A.  Yes, DAR.
Q.  So when you said you were DAR's designated point of
contact for all commercial and contractual matters with
CQBC, you were also DAR's designated point of contact
for all commercial and contractual matters with TCCC and
Msheireb as well?
A.  For all Doha-related operations, I was the point of
contact.
Q.  So is DAR in dispute with TCCC with respect to this
package?
A.  This package, initially it was quoted 52 million if
I remember.  Then it was negotiated with the top
management of Msheireb.  It reached to 40 million.  Then
it was tracked more, more, so right now we are talking
about 29.5 and performed by DAR during TCCC tenure of
10.8 million.  So together it is reaching to 39, which
is almost near to 40 million.  Plus the ACC form, which
is the variation issued by the employer to TCCC.  They
are calling it authorisation of contractor cost.
4.3 million is written for that one.  But it never
happened.  This is the letter of intent which we are
commenting.
Q.  Sorry, I'll just repeat the question.  Is DAR in dispute
with TCCC regarding this package currently?  Are you
currently in dispute with them?
A.  No, the package is closed.  There is no dispute now.
Q.  So there was no litigation, no arbitration in that
regard?
A.  No.
Q.  "Yes" or "no"?
A.  There is no arbitration, there is no litigation.  The
project of remaining work at phase 1B done by TCCC it
was mutually agreed, final account signed and payment
received.
Q.  When was the final account signed?
A.  Exact year I don't recall, but it was 2019 or 2020.
Exact date I cannot recall.
Q.  Did you receive a taking over certificate from TCCC?
A.  We received taking over certificate by the employer.
Q.  Why do you not mention that in your statement?
A.  It was an activity after the termination of CQBC.  My
focus is mainly related to the CQBC activities.
Q.  Did you receive a release of retention from TCCC?
A.  There was -- if I recall in this package, there was no
retention even.
Q.  I'm going to ask you, did you receive a release of
retention from TCCC or you don't know?
A.  If I recall, in the package which we signed with TCCC,
after termination, there was no guarantee and there was
no retention.  If it was there, it is received.  All the
money for that package is received.
Q.  When you say -- I'm just looking at your words carefully
and it's not a criticism.  You say "if I recall", so
that suggests you haven't checked, you're just trying to
work off your memory.  You haven't checked if you
received retention or if you ...
A.  Related to the package which we signed with TCCC,
100 per cent payment is received.  But it is not include
anything which is -- they were calling it "legacy",
"legacy" meaning our engagement with CQBC in the past.
They put a name "legacy".
Q.  When you prepared your statement, or even today, have
you checked the status of the account with TCCC?
Because you don't seem to remember the date of the
taking over certificate, et cetera.  Is that something
you've checked?  If you haven't checked it, just say so.
A.  No, I did not recently check, but at the time when
I write my witness statement, at that time, I reconcile
the things.
Q.  But you don't mention any of this in your statement, so
what are you saying -- what do you mean by you
"reconciled"?  What does that mean?
A.  "Reconciled" meaning whenever I was getting a number,
I was checking the records.  I was talking with the
people who were engaged with me.
By that time, my accountant, Rajesh, my QS Mikthath,
and even Roshan is no more working in Dar Al Rokham, but
I called him to get the information, if I could get.  My
storekeeper, Sajith Kathrie(?).
I talked to all these people when I was drafting my
witness statement.
Q.  Did you ask to see a full list of payments, the final
account, the taking over certificate received from TCCC?
